resources.string: A parent-controlled screen lock that blocks accidental touches — for supervised kids\' use or hands-free video calls.
Touch Lock needs permission to draw over other apps in order to block touch input.
You should switch to the app you want to protect (e.g., YouTube, video call, etc.) before locking the screen.
Touch input is currently disabled. Unlock Touch Lock from the notification to use the app again.
1. The Touch Lock notification is always available in your notification drawer.
2. Open your video, call, or any app you want to protect from accidental touches.
3. Pull down the notification drawer and tap the Touch Lock notification.
4. One tap locks or unlocks instantly - no expansion needed!
Notifications are disabled for Touch Lock. Enable them to lock/unlock from the notification drawer.
The Touch Lock notification channel is blocked. Enable it to lock/unlock from the notification drawer.

Used only while Touch Lock is active, to block navigation bar taps, dismiss an opened notification shade, and bring the protected app back to the front if you navigate away. Never reads or shares what\'s on your screen.
Also block navigation bar taps and auto-return to the locked app if it\'s swiped away. Optional, off by default, and not a substitute for supervision.

Toddler-Proof Lock uses an Android Accessibility service to reinforce Touch Lock while it\'s active: it blocks taps on the navigation bar (Home, Back, Recents), closes the notification shade if it\'s pulled down, and brings the protected app back to the front if it\'s navigated away from.

While active, the service receives window-change events containing the package name of the app currently in the foreground (for example, \"com.google.android.youtube\"). It does not read text, images, or any other on-screen content, and it does not require touch-exploration or screen-content access.
This information is used only to keep the protected app in front while Touch Lock is active. It is processed entirely on your device and is never transmitted, stored remotely, or shared with anyone.
On the next screen, turn on the main toggle only. Skip \"Shortcut\" — enabling it would let Touch Lock be turned off with a quick volume-button press, defeating the point of Toddler-Proof Lock.

Toddler-Proof Lock is a safety aid, not a substitute for supervision. No lock can guarantee that every tap, swipe, or hardware button press is blocked on every device. Keep your child within sight and hearing while the device is locked, the same as with any screen you hand them.
